A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADC framework and AdcSR model, with matching main experiments. The complete text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's added supplementary Sections A–D; v1 contains no supplementary section.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original super-resolution comparisons, efficiency measurements and component ablations, including Tables 1–7.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by additional ablations, benchmark results, an expert preference study and mobile-device measurements.

M1.justification: Structural compression, pruning ratios, two-stage training, feature-space distillation and inference remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure, including discriminator updates; mobile quantization is an additional evaluation setting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets and evaluate 4× super-resolution on DIV2K-Val, DRealSR and RealSR. The added benchmark tables, ratings of existing DIV2K-Val images and mobile measurements extend evaluation procedures and results within this coverage.

E2.justification: Table C.2 and Figures C.2–C.4 add actual comparisons with BSRGAN, Real-ESRGAN, LDL and FeMASR, extending the diffusion-only benchmark comparison to GAN methods. All eight original diffusion baselines remain. Table B.1 also evaluates alternative compression strategies.

E3.justification: Existing training and benchmark settings remain unchanged. New protocols include 32 expert raters judging 16 images using perceptual quality and content consistency, and mobile evaluation on the Qualcomm SM8750 Hexagon DSP using the Qualcomm SDK and W8A16 quantization, with latency, memory and storage measurements.

E4.justification: Tables B.1–B.2 add substantive tests of channel pruning against block removal and tiny-VAE decoding, plus discriminator LoRA ranks, first-layer finetuning and full-discriminator finetuning. These examine compression alternatives and training stability beyond the retained component ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new user study reports vote totals and percentages without uncertainty estimates; its participant count is an evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical values, while the supplement adds extensive benchmark, ablation and qualitative results. New findings include preference rates of 31% for AdcSR, 29% for OSEDiff and 33% for S3Diff, and mobile latencies of 65 ms versus 1647 ms for AdcSR and OSEDiff. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements between versions under the original settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(5) remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 spells out the already described adversarial optimization, including the standard discriminator loss, without adding substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, five stated contributions and conclusion retain the same compression framework, competitive-quality claim and headline efficiency claims, including up to 9.3× acceleration over previous one-step methods. Supplementary evidence supports these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: The supplement adds a proposed explanation for tiny-VAE degradation through reduced depth and lack of a global receptive field, and discusses GAN fidelity versus diffusion perceptual quality. The existing limitations concerning fine textures and heavily degraded details remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promise of future code/model release with stated availability and a concrete repository link. It also adds training/inference pseudocode with discriminator-update details, specific compression-model resources, and mobile hardware, SDK and quantization information, substantially expanding reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including SwiftBrush v2, PAGODA, compression-model resources and several restoration/compressed-sensing works. The related-work organization and central positioning of ADC relative to diffusion distillation and structural compression remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved, with limited wording edits, affiliation and corresponding-author updates, and a supplementary-material pointer. New material is organized into Sections A–D without extensively rewriting the existing exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, Tables B.1–B.2 and C.1–C.3, and Figures C.1–C.4. These introduce a substantial three-dataset comparison table, additional image-comparison grids, study thumbnails and new experimental displays. Existing main figures and tables are retained with minor layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v1 motivates mobile deployment but provides only A100 efficiency measurements and limits its main quantitative baseline comparison to diffusion methods on DRealSR. v2 substantially strengthens validation through actual mobile measurements, GAN comparisons, fuller results across the existing datasets, and tests of compression and discriminator choices. Pseudocode and the stated code/model release also improve reproducibility information. The user study remains descriptive without uncertainty estimates, but the added evidence resolves important gaps in practical and comparative validation.
